target_customer: Advertisers and video marketers buying promoted video views, and publishers hosting the video units
problem: Brands and video producers wanted their videos to reach large audiences without relying on organic virality.
business_model: Self-serve video advertising platform, pay per view or campaign (campaigns from $10 in 2013)

founders.name: Alexander Debelov
previous_startups: A video contest startup for brands (name not given in source)
founders.background_notes: Per TechCrunch his earlier startup ran video contests for brands and clients asked how to make videos go viral.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ad serving across a network of publishers, targeting and reporting at scale; standard adtech engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Publisher network and audience data (450M profiles claimed later) helped, but video ad networks were crowded and advertisers could multi-home.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying it directly; the company was acquired by Turgo in October 2017, though aggregators claim Google or Verizon, which are unverified.

market_need_then: By February 2013 registered advertisers had grown from 200 to 30,000 after the March 2012 self-serve launch, with 20,442 videos promoted and brands including Samsung and Intel running campaigns.

branding.name_origin: A play on the word viral; Debelov told AdExchanger he does not promise advertisers viral results.

identity.voice_and_tone: Marketing language about making advertising human and distributing advertainment

branding.community_and_virality: Trade and tech press covered the funding rounds; the company claimed the biggest YC seed ever (the claim is the company's own).

brand_strength.rationale: Press on the record seed round and a memorable pun, but no consumer community or brand-driven growth evidence.

outcome_analysis: Virool scaled quickly after a March 2012 self-serve launch, raised a record YC seed of $6.62M in 2013 and a $12M Series A in April 2016, then was acquired in October 2017 by Turgo with undisclosed terms. Total raised is about $18.6M by the company's own figure, so the sale looks modest relative to funding, but price and reason are not public.
notes: Business Wire release returned 403; the Series A is confirmed by search results from TechCrunch, MediaPost and the release listing. VentureBeat said the seed was raised entirely as convertible debt; one outlet said $7M. No competitors were named in dated launch coverage, so the list is empty. TechCrunch calls Vlad Gurgov a co-founder but the YC page lists only Debelov, so he is not listed. Acquirer claims conflict: Turgo (Dealroom, La French Tech), Google 2016, Verizon Media, PE; only Turgo has two sources and is used. Website virool.com still operates with product pages.
